'''Marvalee Hendricks Wake''' (born July 31, 1939) is an American zoologist and professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], known for her research in the biology of [[caecilian]]s (limbless amphibians) and vertebrate development and evolution. A 1988 [[Guggenheim Fellow]], she has served as president of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]], the [[American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists]], [[Society for Integrative and Comparative Biology]], [[International Union of Biological Sciences]], and the International Society of Vertebrate Morphology.<ref name=Schwenketal2005>{{cite journal|last1=Schwenk|first1=Kurt|last2=Korff|first2=Wyatt|last3=Matthias Starck|first3=J.|title=Integrative organismal biology: Papers in honor of Professor Marvalee H. Wake|journal=Zoology|date=2005|volume=108|issue=4|pages=261–267|doi=10.1016/j.zool.2005.09.002|pmid=16351974|bibcode=2005Zool..108..261S |url=http://hydrodictyon.eeb.uconn.edu/people/schwenk/SchwenkEAMHWpreface05.pdf|access-date=2015-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304194754/http://hydrodictyon.eeb.uconn.edu/people/schwenk/SchwenkEAMHWpreface05.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-04|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=Hall2005>{{cite journal|last1=Hall|first1=Brian K.|authorlink1 = Brian K. Hall|title=In Goethe's Wake: Marvalee Wake's conceptual contributions to the development and evolution of a science of morphology|journal=Zoology|date=2005|volume=108|issue=4|pages=269–275|doi=10.1016/j.zool.2005.09.005|pmid=16351975}}</ref> She is a [[fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[California Academy of Sciences]], and is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

==Life==
Marvalee Hendricks was born in [[Orange, California]] on July 31, 1939.<ref>{{cite book |title=American Men & Women of Science : Physical and Biological Sciences |url=https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen08newy |url-access=registration |date=1979 |publisher=R. R. Bowker & Company |location=New York |isbn=0835211193 |page=5327 |edition=14th}}</ref> She attended the [[University of Southern California]] (USC), earning a B.A. in 1961; M.S. in 1964; and completing her Ph.D. in 1968 under herpetologist [[Jay Savage]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=https://ib.berkeley.edu/labs/mwake/curriculum.html|title=Dr. Marvalee H. Wake, Curriculum Vitae|work=The Lab of Marvalee H. Wake|publisher=University of California, Berkeley|accessdate=1 November 2015}}</ref> While at USC she met and married biologist [[David B. Wake]] and gave birth to a son. Wake became assistant professor at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]], and later she and her husband moved to the University of California, Berkeley, where David assumed directorship of the [[Museum of Vertebrate Zoology]] and Marvalee became a professor. She was rapidly promoted, eventually assuming the chair of the Department of Zoology and its successor, the Department of Integrative Biology.<ref name=Schwenketal2005/> She nominally retired as professor in 2003, but remained active in research and since 2004 has held the position of Professor of the Graduate School at UC Berkeley.<ref name=Schwenketal2005/><ref name="CV"/>

Wake is known as an expert in [[caecilian]]s—a relatively little-known group of limbless amphibians—and her research has included the developmental biology, evolution, reproduction, and anatomy of these creatures.<ref name="Beolensetal2011"/><ref name=Frost2015/> Her research has been credited with stimulating renewed world-wide interest in the group which has historically received little research.<ref name=Schwenketal2005/> In her doctoral dissertation and a series of early papers she explored comparative aspects of caecilian reproductive anatomy, and in 1972 co-described the first evidence of caecilians in the fossil record.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Estes|first1=Richard|last2=Wake|first2=Marvalee H.|title=The first fossil record of caecilian amphibians|journal=Nature|date=1972|volume=239|issue=5369|pages=228–231|doi=10.1038/239228b0|bibcode=1972Natur.239..228E|s2cid=4260251}}</ref> She is also recognized for her contributions towards the field of vertebrate [[Morphology (biology)|morphology]]. Biologist [[Brian K. Hall]] writes: "Consistently, passionately and effectively, Marvalee Wake has advocated the teaching of morphology as a multifaceted modern science that informs evolutionary biology and evolutionary theory, and is foundational to integrative biology."<ref name=Hall2005/>{{rp|271}} She has formally collaborated with her husband—an expert in salamanders—since 1975, although the two maintain separate labs and graduate students.<ref name="DavidBWake2010">{{cite journal|last1 = Wake|first1 = David B.|author-link = David B. Wake|title = BIO|journal = Evolution & Development|date = 2010|volume = 12|issue = 3|pages = 244–245|doi = 10.1111/j.1525-142X.2010.00409.x|pmid = 20565534|s2cid = 221679002|url = https://ib.berkeley.edu/labs/wake/367_DBWake_Bio.pdf}}</ref>

Wake has published or co-published over 200 journal articles and book chapters, edited a revision of the textbook ''Hyman's Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy'' (originally written by [[Libbie Hyman|Libbie H. Hyman]]), and co-edited a general biology textbook (''Biology'', 1979) as well as the scholarly book ''The Origin and Evolution of Larval Forms'' (1999).<ref name=Schwenketal2005/>

Wake is commemorated in the name of the caecilian ''[[Microcaecilia| Microcaecilia marvaleewakeae]]'',<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Maciel|first1=Adriano O.|last2=Hoogmoed|first2=Marinus S.|authorlink2=:fr:Marinus Steven Hoogmoed|title=A new species of ''Microcaecilia'' (Amphibia: Gymnophiona: Siphonopidae) from the Guianan region of Brazil|journal=Zootaxa|date=2013|volume=3693|issue=3|pages=387–94|doi=10.11646/zootaxa.3693.3.9|pmid=26185857|url=https://www.academia.edu/4622480|quote=It is with great pleasure that we name this species in honor of Dr. Marvalee H. Wake... one of the most important present day researchers of caecilians and author of many publications on development, morphology, phylogeny, and reproductive biology of these secretive animals.}}</ref> and she and her husband are jointly commemorated in the names of the frog genus ''[[Wakea (genus)|Wakea]]''<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Glaw|first1=Frank|authorlink1=Frank Glaw|last2=Vences|first2=Miguel|authorlink2=Miguel Vences|title=Phylogeny and genus-level classification of mantellid frogs (Amphibia, Anura)|journal=Organisms Diversity & Evolution|date=2006|volume=6|issue=3|pages=236–253|doi=10.1016/j.ode.2005.12.001|bibcode=2006ODivE...6..236G |quote=We are pleased to dedicate this genus to David and Marvalee Wake, Berkeley, in recognition of their outstanding contributions to the understanding of amphibian biology.|doi-access=free}}</ref> and the lizard ''[[Cyrtodactylus wakeorum]]'' (Wakes' gecko).<ref name="Beolensetal2011">{{cite book|first1=Bo|last1= Beolens|first2=Michael|last2= Watkins|first3=Michael|last3= Grayson|title=The Eponym Dictionary of Reptiles|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3ovZoFyLhzkC&pg=PT278|year=2011|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|isbn=978-1-4214-0135-5|pages=278–279}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Bauer|first=Aaron M.|author-link=:fr:Aaron Matthew Bauer|year=2003|title= Descriptions of seven new ''Cyrtodactylus'' (Squamata: Gekkonidae) with a key to the species of Myanmar (Burma)|journal=Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences|volume= 54|number=25|pages= 463–498|url=https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/Herpetology/myanmar/PDFS/proccas_v54_n25.pdf|quote=for their contributions to herpetology, vertebrate morphology, and evolutionary biology and for their valuable mentoring of many graduate students}}</ref> A [[festschrift]] of papers in her honor was published in the journal ''[[Zoology (journal)|Zoology]]'' in 2005.<ref name=Schwenketal2005/>

Since 2013, Wake has been listed on the Advisory Council of the [[National Center for Science Education]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ncse.com/about/advisory-council |title=Advisory Council |website=ncse.com |publisher=[[National Center for Science Education]] |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810112828/https://ncse.com/about/advisory-council |archivedate=2013-08-10 |accessdate=2018-10-30}}</ref>

Wake has served as advisor to 17 doctoral students and 15 post-doctoral students. In 2014 she received the Henry S. Fitch Award for Excellence in Herpetology from the [[American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists]].<ref name=Frost2015>{{cite journal|last1=Frost|first1=Darrel|author-link=Darrel R. Frost|title=Marvalee H. Wake: Henry S. Fitch Award for Excellence in Herpetology—2014|journal=Copeia|date=2015|volume=103|issue=1|page=2|doi=10.1643/OT-15-252|s2cid=198150148}}</ref>
